title: The point fibre functor preserves derived tensor at all coefficient stages
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $a\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_{p^a}$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $\ell\ne p$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension inside a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, let $\mathcal O_E$ be its valuation ring and $\varpi_E$ a uniformizer, and let $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Use the point coefficient categories and the functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], the finite-Tor subcategory of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and the derived tensor product of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], completed at the integral stage and formed at a common finite coefficient stage at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. For $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
\operatorname{Fib}_s(M\otimes^L_\Lambda N)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\operatorname{Fib}_s(M)\otimes^L_\Lambda\operatorname{Fib}_s(N).
$$
It is natural in $M,N$, carries the coefficient unit to $\Lambda$, and respects the associativity, symmetry and unit constraints of derived tensor. It commutes with finite reduction and scalar extension in these coefficient constructions.

source.place: Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product (the finite-level geometric fibre case); at the integral, rational and common finite-field stages use the coefficient constructions of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point and def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom.

proof.text: Identify evaluation with an actual inverse-image functor before invoking the tensor theorem. Take the geometric point $\bar s=\mathrm{id}_s$ and the pointed-neighbourhood category of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. For every $(U,u)$, the lift $u:s\to U$ is the unique pointed morphism $(s,\mathrm{id})\to(U,u)$; hence $(s,\mathrm{id})$ is initial in that category and terminal in its opposite. Its colimit is therefore $\mathcal F(s)$: the inverse sends a section over $(U,u)$ to its restriction along $u$, and the colimit relations make this inverse to the map from $\mathcal F(s)$. Thus the topos point furnished by [lem-fix-geometric-stalk-topos-point] has $p^{-1}=\Gamma(s,-)$. For finite coefficients its ring stalk is $A$ by [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk]. For $R_s=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\varprojlim_j(A_{E,j})_s$, sectionwise limits give $p^{-1}R_s=R_s(s)=\varprojlim_j A_{E,j}=\mathcal O_E$; the last equality is the coefficient identification used in [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness](2). Equip this point with the identity ring map to the indicated coefficient ring. Its module pullback is $A\otimes_A\Gamma(s,-)$, or $\mathcal O_E\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\Gamma(s,-)$, and multiplication identifies it with sections.

proof.text: Sections is exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For a K-flat flat-term resolution $P\to K$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback] computes $Lp^*K$ by $p^*P=\Gamma(s,P)$; exactness makes $\Gamma(s,P)\to\Gamma(s,K)$ a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of its canonical comparison with termwise pullback identifies $Lp^*$ with sections on the derived category. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to this ringed point, not to a scheme map $s\to s$. Its canonical bifunctorial isomorphism gives $\Gamma(s,M\otimes^L_A N)\cong\Gamma(s,M)\otimes^L_A\Gamma(s,N)$ at finite coefficients; [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] identifies these with the three fibre objects. Since $s$ is a finite-type $k$-scheme, [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii) puts the input tensor in $D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$. The same ringed-point theorem also supplies the comparison for the ordinary ambient derived tensor of $R_s$-modules; completion at the integral stage still needs the next three steps.

proof.text: Sections commutes with the strict derived limits used here. Countable products of $R_s$-module sheaves are exact and sectionwise by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]; countable products of ordinary $\mathcal O_E$-modules are exact since coordinatewise lifts of a tuple along surjections give a lift. By [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core], the products in both derived categories are termwise products. Sections therefore carries the product and the transition endomorphism $1-t$ of a strict tower to the corresponding module product and $1-t$. In the natural Roos triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], the derived limit is represented by the shifted cone of this chain map. Applying exact sections termwise preserves that cone, including its differential and projections. Consequently $\Gamma(s,R\varprojlim_j T_j)\cong R\varprojlim_j\Gamma(s,T_j)$ naturally for the strict reduction/tensor towers; this uses the functorial cone model, not an arbitrary lift into a triangulated derived limit.

source.place: Tag 07KC, derived.tex lemma-products; Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, product/cone calculation

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $C=\operatorname{Fib}_s(M)$ and $D=\operatorname{Fib}_s(N)$ for integral $M,N$. By [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness](2), $C,D$ have bounded finitely generated cohomology. The DVR clause of [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius] makes each perfect, so choose bounded finite-projective module models $P,Q$ as in [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Their total tensor $V=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)$ is again bounded finite projective: projectives are direct summands of finite free modules, so each $P^i\otimes_RQ^j$ is a direct summand of a finite free module. It computes $C\otimes_R^L D$. The canonical completion map $V\to R\varprojlim_j(V\otimes_R A_{E,j})$ is an isomorphism. Indeed every term of $V$ is a direct summand of $R^h$; $R=\varprojlim_j A_{E,j}$ gives the same equality for each such summand and every differential. The quotient transitions are surjective termwise, so $1-t$ on the product complexes is surjective termwise (solve $x_j-t_jx_{j+1}=y_j$ recursively using these surjections), with kernel the termwise inverse limit $V$. Its cone shifted by $-1$ is therefore quasi-isomorphic to $V$. This proves completion for the ordinary module tensor actually appearing on the right of the item.

source.place: Coefficient construction of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point; bounded perfect models and the product/cone model of Tag 0941

proof.text:
Write $M_j=M\otimes_R^L A_{E,j}$ and $N_j=N\otimes_R^L A_{E,j}$. They are finite-Tor objects by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The integral tensor of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is the strict derived limit of $M_j\otimes^L_{A_{E,j}}N_j$ with restriction of scalars. It is constructible, and its reductions are those tensors, by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible](2). Step 3 evaluates this limit. Step 2 and [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] identify its evaluated tower, with its quotient transition maps, with
$$ (C\otimes_R^L A_{E,j})\otimes^L_{A_{E,j}}(D\otimes_R^L A_{E,j})=(C\otimes_R^L D)\otimes_R^L A_{E,j}. $$
The equality is the derived base-change associator: on flat-term models it is $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$. Thus it commutes with each quotient map $A_{E,j+1}\to A_{E,j}$. Take the functorial derived limit of this tower identification and compose with the inverse of the canonical completion isomorphism in step 4. This gives $\operatorname{Fib}_s(M\widehat\otimes_R^L N)\cong C\otimes_R^L D$ in the asserted direction. All maps used are natural; inverses of their isomorphisms are natural, so the integral comparison is natural too. This proves the integral case without identifying completed sheaf tensor with ordinary module tensor by definition.

source.place: Tag 07A4 on finite reductions; integral completed-tensor definition and canonical reduction comparisons

proof.text:
For the rational stage use the integral presentations required by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; they may be arbitrary integral constructible objects, since [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] identifies $D^b_c(s,R)=D^b_{ctf}(s,R)$, so step 5 applies to these presentations. The ring $E=R[1/\varpi_E]$ is flat over $R$: localization of a kernel is its localized kernel, since a numerator mapping to zero is killed by some denominator. On the bounded projective models $P,Q$ in step 4, the balanced map
$$ (P\otimes_RQ)\otimes_RE\longrightarrow (P\otimes_RE)\otimes_E(Q\otimes_RE),\quad (x\otimes y)\otimes c\longmapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes(y\otimes c) $$
has inverse $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)\mapsto(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$ and commutes with the tensor differential. Tensoring the integral comparison with $E$ and applying this isomorphism gives the rational comparison. For morphisms represented by $f\otimes a$ and $g\otimes b$, integral naturality tensored with $E$ gives the naturality square multiplied by $ab$, which is precisely rational naturality under the stated definitions.

source.place: Rationalization clauses of the two coefficient definitions; balanced tensor base-change calculation

proof.text:
For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, choose representatives $(E_1,M_1),(E_2,N_2)$ and let $L=E_1E_2$ inside the fixed algebraic closure. Write $M_L=M_1\otimes_{E_1}L$ and $N_L=N_2\otimes_{E_2}L$. Apply step 6 over $L$ to obtain
$$ \operatorname{Fib}_s(M_L\otimes_L^L N_L)\cong\operatorname{Fib}_s(M_L)\otimes_L^L\operatorname{Fib}_s(N_L). $$
On the right compose with $\varphi_{L/E_1,M_1}\otimes\varphi_{L/E_2,N_2}$ from [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], in its rational form. The resulting arrow over $L$ has exactly the source and target of the common-stage tensor and fibre definitions. Upon extension to $L'\supset L$, the tensor comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] and the composition equation for $\varphi$ identify each of its three factors with the corresponding factor formed over $L'$: the balanced tensor rule is multiplication of the two new scalars, as in step 6. For two choices of representatives or common field, pass to a field containing both; these equalities identify the arrows there, hence their classes in the 2-colimit. For a pair of morphisms, represent both over such a field and apply rational naturality there. This proves independence and naturality, with the actual comparison arrows specified.

source.place: Common-stage clauses of def-weil-finite-coefficient-point and def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, with their scalar associator comparisons

proof.text: Check the tensor constraints on the canonical comparisons rather than only their objectwise invertibility. At the ambient finite or integral ringed-point level, choose K-flat flat-term representatives as allowed by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. The module comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] sends tensor generators to the tensor of their images. In a triple tensor, both associativity composites send $(x\otimes y)\otimes z$ to the images of $x,y,z$ in that order, after the associator. In degrees $i,j$, the two symmetry composites both send $x\otimes y$ to $(-1)^{ij}$ times the images of $y\otimes x$. With the unit, the two composites send $a\otimes x$ to $a$ times the image of $x$. These are equalities of balanced module maps in each bidegree; they commute with differentials and sums in totalization, so are equalities of complex maps. The resolving-class uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] descends them to the derived categories. At the integral completed stage perform the same identities on every finite reduction and take the functorial limit of their equal chain maps as in steps 3--5; the completion map of step 4 preserves these identities by its quotient projections. Tensoring those equations with $E$ proves them in step 6, and applying them over a common field proves them in step 7. The unit is evaluated as $A$, $R$, $E$, or its common-stage class, by step 1 and the coefficient definitions. Thus all four comparisons respect unit, associativity and symmetry.

source.place: Tag 07A4 proof, total-complex comparison; Tag 03EL module tensor comparison; Tag 06YU resolving-class descent

proof.text: For reduction or scalar change $A\to B$, the square comparing tensor before and after change of coefficients commutes on flat-term models: its two paths on $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)$ give $(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$. This is the change-of-rings associator of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the canonical tensor comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Its equality survives resolving-class localization by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. At the integral stage, the reduction comparison of [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] is the canonical one, obtained from the cone of multiplication by $\varpi_E^j$; exact sections sends that multiplication and its cone to the identical module multiplication and cone. Therefore its square with these tensor maps is the just-checked finite square, and steps 3--5 use exactly those quotient projections. For a finite field extension $E\subset L$, [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] gives the source completed-tensor comparison, and [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] identifies the fibre comparison with the inverse of the canonical sections-tensor map followed by completion. On flat-term models their tensor square is again the displayed balanced rule with $B=\mathcal O_L$; at the completed stage it is obtained from that rule on its finite quotients. Their stipulated identity and composition equations give the identity-extension and iterated-extension squares. Finally tensor these equations with the fraction field and take their common-stage classes. This proves the finite reduction and scalar extension compatibilities asserted in the item, including the independence invoked in step 7.
